#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml

#        with the fail-closed select(.conclusion == "success") projection.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi

# Portable ISO-UTC timestamp <secs> ago (GNU date on CI; BSD date locally).
iso_ago() {
  if date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  else
    date -u -j -v -"$1"S '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "${GH_CALL_LOG:?GH_CALL_LOG required}"

fi
fixture="${GH_STUB_FIXTURE:?GH_STUB_FIXTURE required}"
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -qF 'select(.conclusion'; then
  grep -o '{[^}]*}' "$fixture" |
    grep '"conclusion":"success"' |
    sed 's/.*"createdAt":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/'
  exit 0

  grep -o '"createdAt":"[^"]*"' "$fixture" |
    sed 's/"createdAt":"//; s/"$//'
  exit 0
fi

chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

RC=0
# run_check <event> <tag> <case-name> — runs the REAL check script against
# the stub with EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME set; the `dedupe=` line lands in
# $TMP/out.<case>, everything the script prints lands in
# $TMP/stdout.<case>, the stub's call log in $TMP/calls.log (fresh per
# case). The script's exit code is left in $RC.
run_check() {
  : > "$TMP/out.$3"
  : > "$TMP/stdout.$3"
  : > "$TMP/calls.log"
  EVENT_NAME="$1" GITHUB_REF_NAME="$2" GH_CALL_LOG="$TMP/calls.log" \
    PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" \
    bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/out.$3" >"$TMP/stdout.$3" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at[:conclusion[:status]]>... —
  # writes the `gh run list --json createdAt,conclusion,status` answer

  # success run (the hot-path answer: behind the shared ci-<ref>
  # concurrency group the push twin finished before the release twin's
  # check executes).
  local name="$1"

    local sep="" row created concl status
    for row in "$@"; do

      concl="${row%%:*}"

releaseDispatch:
        description: 'gh-1172: real release (cuts the annotated tag + GitHub Release directly, gh-1522) on manual dispatch — requires refs/heads/main; bare validation dispatches stay inert'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
  # Any release publication (API `gh release create`, web UI, or a pushed
  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg to the binaries-attach leg when the tag's push run
  # already gates it (the retired comment here only made the binaries
  # UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create + --clobber, last wins — while
  # the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran, doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# Superseded PR runs die instantly (issue #177 wave 1). Tag/schedule
# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

#   DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts the tag
#   and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds the
#   stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg
#       (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins);
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — any status dedupes (no status filter is
  # passed: in the hot path the push twin is still in_progress) and no
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt \
      --jq '.[].createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips the quality gate and executes the binaries-attach leg only (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1625
# release-dedupe pre-check (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh, the
# release-dedupe job in ci.yml).
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate; the `release: published`
# event for the same tag used to fire a second identical gate. The check
# must dedupe exactly the fresh-twin case and fail safe everywhere else.
# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no token):
#   AC1  a recent push run for the tag (ANY status — the stub contract
#        pins that the script passes no --status filter) dedupes: the
#        release twin skips the gate, binaries-attach only;
#   AC2  no recent push run (an old tag's release, or a tag the release
#        created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) does NOT
#        dedupe: the full gate stays the safety net;
#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml
#        --branch <tag> --event push.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# Portable ISO-UTC timestamp <secs> ago (GNU date on CI; BSD date locally).
iso_ago() {
  if date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  else
    date -u -j -v -"$1"S '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  fi
}

# Stub `gh`: serves the GH_STUB_FIXTURE JSON file as the `gh run list`
# answer (unless GH_STUB_FAIL is set — then it fails like a red API) and
# records every invocation to GH_CALL_LOG. Emulates the ONE jq projection
# the check uses (`--jq '.[].createdAt'` — one timestamp per line), the
# same faithful-stub discipline as flake_watch_selftest.sh's search quirk.
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
cat > "$TMP/bin/gh" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "${GH_CALL_LOG:?GH_CALL_LOG required}"
if [ -n "${GH_STUB_FAIL:-}" ]; then
  echo "gh: The deployment API is experiencing problems (stub)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
fixture="${GH_STUB_FIXTURE:?GH_STUB_FIXTURE required}"
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -q -- '--jq .\[\].createdAt'; then
  grep -o '"createdAt":"[^"]*"' "$fixture" |
    sed 's/"createdAt":"//; s/"$//'
else
  cat "$fixture"
fi
STUB
chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

RC=0
# run_check <event> <tag> <case-name> — runs the REAL check script against
# the stub with EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME set; the `dedupe=` line lands in
# $TMP/out.<case>, everything the script prints lands in
# $TMP/stdout.<case>, the stub's call log in $TMP/calls.log (fresh per
# case). The script's exit code is left in $RC.
run_check() {
  : > "$TMP/out.$3"
  : > "$TMP/stdout.$3"
  : > "$TMP/calls.log"
  EVENT_NAME="$1" GITHUB_REF_NAME="$2" GH_CALL_LOG="$TMP/calls.log" \
    PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" \
    bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/out.$3" >"$TMP/stdout.$3" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at rows...> — writes the
  # `gh run list --json createdAt` answer shape and prints its path.
  local name="$1"
  shift
  {
    printf '['
    local sep="" row
    for row in "$@"; do
      printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s"}' "$sep" "$row"
      sep=', '
    done
    printf ']\n'
  } > "$TMP/fx.$name"
  printf '%s' "$TMP/fx.$name"
}

# ── AC1: a fresh push twin dedupes the release twin ─────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture recent "$(iso_ago 60)")" run_check release vTest.0 fresh
check 'AC1: recent push run → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"
check 'AC1: the script exits 0 (the short-circuit is green, never red)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters this workflow (--workflow ci.yml)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--workflow ci.yml' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup keys on the tag ref (--branch <tag>)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--branch vTest.0' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters the push event (--event push)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--event push' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: no --status filter — ANY status dedupes (the push twin is still in_progress in the hot path)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--status' "$TMP/calls.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
check 'RG: the output file carries EXACTLY the dedupe line (annotations never pollute GITHUB_OUTPUT)' \
  "$(printf 'dedupe=true\n' | cmp -s - "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1: 2+ runs, one stale + one recent — the recent one still dedupes ──
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture mixed "$(iso_ago 100000)" "$(iso_ago 120)")" \
  run_check release vTest.0 mixed
check 'AC1: a recent run among stale ones → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.mixed"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1/AC2: the window boundary (default 6h) is honored ────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-in "$(iso_ago 21570)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-in
check 'AC1: a run seconds inside the window still dedupes' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.edge-in"; echo $?)"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-out "$(iso_ago 21630)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-out
check 'AC2: a run just past the window does NOT dedupe' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.edge-out"; echo $?)"

# ── AC2: the old-tag safety net ──────────────────────────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture old "$(iso_ago 100000)")" run_check release vOld.0 old
check 'AC2: only stale push runs (old-tag release) → dedupe=false, the full gate runs' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.old"; echo $?)"

printf '[]\n' > "$TMP/fx.empty"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vNew.0 empty
check 'AC2: no push run at all (release-created tag) → dedupe=false' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.empty"; echo $?)"

# ── AC3: non-release arms never call the API ─────────────────────────────
for ev in push schedule workflow_dispatch; do
  GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check "$ev" vTest.0 "arm-$ev"
  check "AC3: $ev arm → dedupe=false" \
    "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.arm-$ev"; echo $?)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm makes NO gh call" \
    "$([ -s "$TMP/calls.log" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm exits 0" \
    "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
done

# ── AC5: an API failure fails safe to the full gate ──────────────────────
GH_STUB_FAIL=1 GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vTest.0 apierr
check 'AC5: gh run list failure → dedupe=false (the gate decides)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the failure warns loudly (::warning::)' \
  "$(grep -q '::warning::' "$TMP/stdout.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the script still exits 0 (the pre-check never reddens the run)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo '✅ release-dedupe self-test green'
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ release-dedupe self-test: $fails failing assertion(s)"
exit 1

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own push run IS the
    # gate — the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522) — a hand-bump desyncs the tag-derived builds. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

# release-dedupe job in ci.yml).
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate; the `release: published`
# event for the same tag used to fire a second identical gate. The check
# must dedupe exactly the fresh-GREEN-twin case and fail safe everywhere
# else. Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no token):
#   AC1  a recent push run for the tag with conclusion == "success"
#        dedupes: the release twin skips every gate leg, the
#        release-specific legs (binaries attach, release-provenance
#        signing, installer smoke) keep running;
#   FC   FAIL-CLOSED (gh-1625 review): a failed/cancelled/in-progress
#        push run does NOT dedupe — the release twin re-runs the full
#        gate, goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing. Behind
#        the shared ci-<ref> concurrency group (cancel-in-progress:
#        false, tag runs never cancelled) the push twin is already
#        completed when the release twin's check executes, so
#        success-only is strictly safe: any other outcome degrades to
#        the AC2 full-gate safety net, never to a skipped gate;
#   AC2  no recent push run (an old tag's release, or a tag the release
#        created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) does NOT
#        dedupe: the full gate stays the safety net;
#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml
#        --branch <tag> --event push, --json createdAt,conclusion,status
#        with the fail-closed select(.conclusion == "success") projection.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# Portable ISO-UTC timestamp <secs> ago (GNU date on CI; BSD date locally).
iso_ago() {
  if date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  else
    date -u -j -v -"$1"S '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  fi

# Stub `gh`: serves the GH_STUB_FIXTURE JSON file as the `gh run list`

#   `.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt` — one createdAt
#       line per GREEN run, every other conclusion filtered out (the

#   `.[].createdAt` — every row, status-blind (the pre-rework projection;
#       served too so a regression of the script redden THIS test, not
#       the next release).
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "${GH_CALL_LOG:?GH_CALL_LOG required}"
if [ -n "${GH_STUB_FAIL:-}" ]; then
  echo "gh: The deployment API is experiencing problems (stub)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
fixture="${GH_STUB_FIXTURE:?GH_STUB_FIXTURE required}"
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -qF 'select(.conclusion'; then
  grep -o '{[^}]*}' "$fixture" |
    grep '"conclusion":"success"' |
    sed 's/.*"createdAt":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/'
  exit 0
fi
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -q -- '--jq .\[\].createdAt'; then
  grep -o '"createdAt":"[^"]*"' "$fixture" |
    sed 's/"createdAt":"//; s/"$//'
  exit 0
fi
cat "$fixture"
STUB
chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

RC=0
# run_check <event> <tag> <case-name> — runs the REAL check script against
# the stub with EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME set; the `dedupe=` line lands in
# $TMP/out.<case>, everything the script prints lands in
# $TMP/stdout.<case>, the stub's call log in $TMP/calls.log (fresh per
# case). The script's exit code is left in $RC.
run_check() {
  : > "$TMP/out.$3"
  : > "$TMP/stdout.$3"
  : > "$TMP/calls.log"
  EVENT_NAME="$1" GITHUB_REF_NAME="$2" GH_CALL_LOG="$TMP/calls.log" \
    PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" \
    bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/out.$3" >"$TMP/stdout.$3" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at[:conclusion[:status]]>... —
  # writes the `gh run list --json createdAt,conclusion,status` answer
  # shape and prints its path. A bare timestamp defaults to a COMPLETED
  # success run (the hot-path answer: behind the shared ci-<ref>
  # concurrency group the push twin finished before the release twin's
  # check executes).
  local name="$1"

    printf '['
    local sep="" row created concl status
    for row in "$@"; do
      created="${row%%:*}"
      if [ "$row" = "$created" ]; then
        printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s","conclusion":"success","status":"COMPLETED"}' "$sep" "$created"

        continue

      concl="${row%%:*}"

        continue

      printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s","conclusion":"%s","status":"%s"}' "$sep" "$created" "$concl" "$status"
      sep=', '
    done

        required: false

  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg to the binaries-attach leg when the tag's push run
  # already gates it (the retired comment here only made the binaries
  # UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create + --clobber, last wins — while
  # the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran, doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with ANY status (queued/in_progress/completed — in the hot path
#   the push twin is still in_progress) created within the last
#   DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts the tag
#   and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds the
#   stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg
#       (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins);
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — any status dedupes (no status filter is
  # passed: in the hot path the push twin is still in_progress) and no
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt \
      --jq '.[].createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips the quality gate and executes the binaries-attach leg only (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1625
# release-dedupe pre-check (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh, the
# release-dedupe job in ci.yml).
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate; the `release: published`
# event for the same tag used to fire a second identical gate. The check
# must dedupe exactly the fresh-twin case and fail safe everywhere else.
# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no token):
#   AC1  a recent push run for the tag (ANY status — the stub contract
#        pins that the script passes no --status filter) dedupes: the
#        release twin skips the gate, binaries-attach only;
#   AC2  no recent push run (an old tag's release, or a tag the release
#        created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) does NOT
#        dedupe: the full gate stays the safety net;
#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml
#        --branch <tag> --event push.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# Portable ISO-UTC timestamp <secs> ago (GNU date on CI; BSD date locally).
iso_ago() {
  if date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  else
    date -u -j -v -"$1"S '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  fi
}

# Stub `gh`: serves the GH_STUB_FIXTURE JSON file as the `gh run list`
# answer (unless GH_STUB_FAIL is set — then it fails like a red API) and
# records every invocation to GH_CALL_LOG. Emulates the ONE jq projection
# the check uses (`--jq '.[].createdAt'` — one timestamp per line), the
# same faithful-stub discipline as flake_watch_selftest.sh's search quirk.
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
cat > "$TMP/bin/gh" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "${GH_CALL_LOG:?GH_CALL_LOG required}"
if [ -n "${GH_STUB_FAIL:-}" ]; then
  echo "gh: The deployment API is experiencing problems (stub)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
fixture="${GH_STUB_FIXTURE:?GH_STUB_FIXTURE required}"
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -q -- '--jq .\[\].createdAt'; then
  grep -o '"createdAt":"[^"]*"' "$fixture" |
    sed 's/"createdAt":"//; s/"$//'
else
  cat "$fixture"
fi
STUB
chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

RC=0
# run_check <event> <tag> <case-name> — runs the REAL check script against
# the stub with EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME set; the `dedupe=` line lands in
# $TMP/out.<case>, everything the script prints lands in
# $TMP/stdout.<case>, the stub's call log in $TMP/calls.log (fresh per
# case). The script's exit code is left in $RC.
run_check() {
  : > "$TMP/out.$3"
  : > "$TMP/stdout.$3"
  : > "$TMP/calls.log"
  EVENT_NAME="$1" GITHUB_REF_NAME="$2" GH_CALL_LOG="$TMP/calls.log" \
    PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" \
    bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/out.$3" >"$TMP/stdout.$3" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at rows...> — writes the
  # `gh run list --json createdAt` answer shape and prints its path.
  local name="$1"
  shift
  {
    printf '['
    local sep="" row
    for row in "$@"; do
      printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s"}' "$sep" "$row"
      sep=', '
    done
    printf ']\n'
  } > "$TMP/fx.$name"
  printf '%s' "$TMP/fx.$name"
}

# ── AC1: a fresh push twin dedupes the release twin ─────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture recent "$(iso_ago 60)")" run_check release vTest.0 fresh
check 'AC1: recent push run → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"
check 'AC1: the script exits 0 (the short-circuit is green, never red)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters this workflow (--workflow ci.yml)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--workflow ci.yml' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup keys on the tag ref (--branch <tag>)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--branch vTest.0' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters the push event (--event push)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--event push' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: no --status filter — ANY status dedupes (the push twin is still in_progress in the hot path)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--status' "$TMP/calls.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
check 'RG: the output file carries EXACTLY the dedupe line (annotations never pollute GITHUB_OUTPUT)' \
  "$(printf 'dedupe=true\n' | cmp -s - "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1: 2+ runs, one stale + one recent — the recent one still dedupes ──
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture mixed "$(iso_ago 100000)" "$(iso_ago 120)")" \
  run_check release vTest.0 mixed
check 'AC1: a recent run among stale ones → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.mixed"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1/AC2: the window boundary (default 6h) is honored ────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-in "$(iso_ago 21570)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-in
check 'AC1: a run seconds inside the window still dedupes' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.edge-in"; echo $?)"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-out "$(iso_ago 21630)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-out
check 'AC2: a run just past the window does NOT dedupe' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.edge-out"; echo $?)"

# ── AC2: the old-tag safety net ──────────────────────────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture old "$(iso_ago 100000)")" run_check release vOld.0 old
check 'AC2: only stale push runs (old-tag release) → dedupe=false, the full gate runs' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.old"; echo $?)"

printf '[]\n' > "$TMP/fx.empty"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vNew.0 empty
check 'AC2: no push run at all (release-created tag) → dedupe=false' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.empty"; echo $?)"

# ── AC3: non-release arms never call the API ─────────────────────────────
for ev in push schedule workflow_dispatch; do
  GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check "$ev" vTest.0 "arm-$ev"
  check "AC3: $ev arm → dedupe=false" \
    "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.arm-$ev"; echo $?)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm makes NO gh call" \
    "$([ -s "$TMP/calls.log" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm exits 0" \
    "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
done

# ── AC5: an API failure fails safe to the full gate ──────────────────────
GH_STUB_FAIL=1 GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vTest.0 apierr
check 'AC5: gh run list failure → dedupe=false (the gate decides)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the failure warns loudly (::warning::)' \
  "$(grep -q '::warning::' "$TMP/stdout.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the script still exits 0 (the pre-check never reddens the run)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo '✅ release-dedupe self-test green'
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ release-dedupe self-test: $fails failing assertion(s)"
exit 1

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own push run IS the
    # gate — the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

    name: Sign release checksums

    done

  } > "$TMP/fx.$name"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with ANY status (queued/in_progress/completed — in the hot path
#   the push twin is still in_progress) created within the last
#   DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts the tag
#   and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds the
#   stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg
#       (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins);
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — any status dedupes (no status filter is
  # passed: in the hot path the push twin is still in_progress) and no
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt \
      --jq '.[].createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips the quality gate and executes the binaries-attach leg only (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1625
# release-dedupe pre-check (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh, the
# release-dedupe job in ci.yml).
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate; the `release: published`
# event for the same tag used to fire a second identical gate. The check
# must dedupe exactly the fresh-twin case and fail safe everywhere else.
# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no token):
#   AC1  a recent push run for the tag (ANY status — the stub contract
#        pins that the script passes no --status filter) dedupes: the
#        release twin skips the gate, binaries-attach only;
#   AC2  no recent push run (an old tag's release, or a tag the release
#        created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) does NOT
#        dedupe: the full gate stays the safety net;
#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml
#        --branch <tag> --event push.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# Portable ISO-UTC timestamp <secs> ago (GNU date on CI; BSD date locally).
iso_ago() {
  if date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  else
    date -u -j -v -"$1"S '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  fi
}

# Stub `gh`: serves the GH_STUB_FIXTURE JSON file as the `gh run list`
# answer (unless GH_STUB_FAIL is set — then it fails like a red API) and
# records every invocation to GH_CALL_LOG. Emulates the ONE jq projection
# the check uses (`--jq '.[].createdAt'` — one timestamp per line), the
# same faithful-stub discipline as flake_watch_selftest.sh's search quirk.
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
cat > "$TMP/bin/gh" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "${GH_CALL_LOG:?GH_CALL_LOG required}"
if [ -n "${GH_STUB_FAIL:-}" ]; then
  echo "gh: The deployment API is experiencing problems (stub)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
fixture="${GH_STUB_FIXTURE:?GH_STUB_FIXTURE required}"
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -q -- '--jq .\[\].createdAt'; then
  grep -o '"createdAt":"[^"]*"' "$fixture" |
    sed 's/"createdAt":"//; s/"$//'
else
  cat "$fixture"
fi
STUB
chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

RC=0
# run_check <event> <tag> <case-name> — runs the REAL check script against
# the stub with EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME set; the `dedupe=` line lands in
# $TMP/out.<case>, everything the script prints lands in
# $TMP/stdout.<case>, the stub's call log in $TMP/calls.log (fresh per
# case). The script's exit code is left in $RC.
run_check() {
  : > "$TMP/out.$3"
  : > "$TMP/stdout.$3"
  : > "$TMP/calls.log"
  EVENT_NAME="$1" GITHUB_REF_NAME="$2" GH_CALL_LOG="$TMP/calls.log" \
    PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" \
    bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/out.$3" >"$TMP/stdout.$3" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at rows...> — writes the
  # `gh run list --json createdAt` answer shape and prints its path.
  local name="$1"
  shift
  {
    printf '['
    local sep="" row
    for row in "$@"; do
      printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s"}' "$sep" "$row"
      sep=', '
    done
    printf ']\n'
  } > "$TMP/fx.$name"
  printf '%s' "$TMP/fx.$name"
}

# ── AC1: a fresh push twin dedupes the release twin ─────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture recent "$(iso_ago 60)")" run_check release vTest.0 fresh
check 'AC1: recent push run → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"
check 'AC1: the script exits 0 (the short-circuit is green, never red)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters this workflow (--workflow ci.yml)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--workflow ci.yml' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup keys on the tag ref (--branch <tag>)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--branch vTest.0' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters the push event (--event push)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--event push' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: no --status filter — ANY status dedupes (the push twin is still in_progress in the hot path)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--status' "$TMP/calls.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
check 'RG: the output file carries EXACTLY the dedupe line (annotations never pollute GITHUB_OUTPUT)' \
  "$(printf 'dedupe=true\n' | cmp -s - "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1: 2+ runs, one stale + one recent — the recent one still dedupes ──
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture mixed "$(iso_ago 100000)" "$(iso_ago 120)")" \
  run_check release vTest.0 mixed
check 'AC1: a recent run among stale ones → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.mixed"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1/AC2: the window boundary (default 6h) is honored ────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-in "$(iso_ago 21570)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-in
check 'AC1: a run seconds inside the window still dedupes' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.edge-in"; echo $?)"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-out "$(iso_ago 21630)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-out
check 'AC2: a run just past the window does NOT dedupe' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.edge-out"; echo $?)"

# ── AC2: the old-tag safety net ──────────────────────────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture old "$(iso_ago 100000)")" run_check release vOld.0 old
check 'AC2: only stale push runs (old-tag release) → dedupe=false, the full gate runs' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.old"; echo $?)"

printf '[]\n' > "$TMP/fx.empty"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vNew.0 empty
check 'AC2: no push run at all (release-created tag) → dedupe=false' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.empty"; echo $?)"

# ── AC3: non-release arms never call the API ─────────────────────────────
for ev in push schedule workflow_dispatch; do
  GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check "$ev" vTest.0 "arm-$ev"
  check "AC3: $ev arm → dedupe=false" \
    "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.arm-$ev"; echo $?)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm makes NO gh call" \
    "$([ -s "$TMP/calls.log" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm exits 0" \
    "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
done

# ── AC5: an API failure fails safe to the full gate ──────────────────────
GH_STUB_FAIL=1 GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vTest.0 apierr
check 'AC5: gh run list failure → dedupe=false (the gate decides)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the failure warns loudly (::warning::)' \
  "$(grep -q '::warning::' "$TMP/stdout.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the script still exits 0 (the pre-check never reddens the run)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo '✅ release-dedupe self-test green'
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ release-dedupe self-test: $fails failing assertion(s)"
exit 1

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own push run IS the
    # gate — the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1

      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder

        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash

            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

release-provenance:
    name: Sign release checksums
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [binaries, web-spa]
    timeout-minutes: 10
    if: >-
      !cancelled() && needs.binaries.result == 'success' &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # upload SHA256SUMS(.sig) to the GitHub Release
    steps:
      # gh-814 r2: the trust-anchor drift gate below diffs the secret's public
      # key against the PEM embedded in site/install.sh — that file must be
      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Collect release assets
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        run: |
          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

      - name: Build and sign SHA256SUMS
        env:
          FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY }}
        run: |
          cd provenance
          sha256sum fa-* > SHA256SUMS
          if [ -z "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            echo "::error::FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY is not set — refusing to publish a release without signed checksums (SEC-07 #795, fail-closed). Set the repo secret with the release-signing private key."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$FA_RELEASE_SIGNING_KEY" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          chmod 600 "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"
          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.
          trap 'rm -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key"' EXIT
          openssl dgst -sha256 -sign "$RUNNER_TEMP/fa-release-signing.key" -out SHA256SUMS.sig SHA256SUMS

  # annotated tag) builds + attaches the binaries matrix. Pushed tags also
  # arrive via the push filter above; the quality gate is NOT re-run by
  # the release twin — the release-dedupe pre-check (gh-1625) short-circuits
  # every gate leg to the binaries-attach leg when the tag's push run
  # already gates it (the retired comment here only made the binaries
  # UPLOAD idempotent — duplicate create + --clobber, last wins — while
  # the full 35-40 min gate still re-ran, doubling release wall time).
  release:
    types: [published]
  schedule:
    # Coalesced auto-release catch-up: when pushes outpace the 2h coalesce
    # window, this releases the pending commits (pub.dev caps ~12 publishes/day).
    # gh-1551: the schedule tick IS the release arming mechanism (gh-1537
    # retired the post-merge main run) — but a tick with zero commits on
    # main since the last v* tag has nothing to release, so the
    # `release-pending` pre-check job short-circuits the whole quality
    # gate in seconds (every leg shows SKIPPED explicitly, the run stays
    # green — never a silent absence, never 35-40 min for an empty tick).
    - cron: '23 */2 * * *'

# runs are never cancelled mid-flight — release flow must not be preempted.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}

#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with ANY status (queued/in_progress/completed — in the hot path
#   the push twin is still in_progress) created within the last
#   DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts the tag
#   and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds the
#   stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       the release twin executes ONLY the binaries-attach leg
#       (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins);
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.

EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

  # ref from the push event — any status dedupes (no status filter is
  # passed: in the hot path the push twin is still in_progress) and no
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).

      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt \
      --jq '.[].createdAt' 2>&1); then

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_selftest.sh — fixture self-test for the gh-1625
# release-dedupe pre-check (scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh, the
# release-dedupe job in ci.yml).
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate; the `release: published`
# event for the same tag used to fire a second identical gate. The check
# must dedupe exactly the fresh-twin case and fail safe everywhere else.
# Proves, on a PATH-stubbed gh (no network, no token):
#   AC1  a recent push run for the tag (ANY status — the stub contract
#        pins that the script passes no --status filter) dedupes: the
#        release twin skips the gate, binaries-attach only;
#   AC2  no recent push run (an old tag's release, or a tag the release
#        created itself — API-created tags fire no push event) does NOT
#        dedupe: the full gate stays the safety net;
#   AC3  non-release arms (push/schedule/workflow_dispatch) short-circuit
#        with NO API call at all;
#   AC5  a failing `gh run list` degrades to dedupe=false with a loud
#        ::warning:: and a zero exit — the gate decides, never the pre-check;
#   RG   the output contract: the output file carries EXACTLY the
#        `dedupe=<bool>` line (annotations go to stdout, never into
#        GITHUB_OUTPUT), and the lookup shape is --workflow ci.yml
#        --branch <tag> --event push.
# Same discipline as sm_merge_guard_selftest.sh (gh-1568, #1100 pattern).
set -u
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CHECK="$HERE/release_dedupe_check.sh"
TMP="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

fails=0
check() { # check <desc> <condition-exit-code: 0 = pass>
  if [ "$2" = "0" ]; then
    echo "  ok: $1"
  else
    echo "  FAIL: $1"
    fails=$((fails + 1))
  fi
}

# Portable ISO-UTC timestamp <secs> ago (GNU date on CI; BSD date locally).
iso_ago() {
  if date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    date -u -d "-$1 seconds" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  else
    date -u -j -v -"$1"S '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ'
  fi
}

# Stub `gh`: serves the GH_STUB_FIXTURE JSON file as the `gh run list`
# answer (unless GH_STUB_FAIL is set — then it fails like a red API) and
# records every invocation to GH_CALL_LOG. Emulates the ONE jq projection
# the check uses (`--jq '.[].createdAt'` — one timestamp per line), the
# same faithful-stub discipline as flake_watch_selftest.sh's search quirk.
mkdir -p "$TMP/bin"
cat > "$TMP/bin/gh" <<'STUB'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
echo "$*" >> "${GH_CALL_LOG:?GH_CALL_LOG required}"
if [ -n "${GH_STUB_FAIL:-}" ]; then
  echo "gh: The deployment API is experiencing problems (stub)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
fixture="${GH_STUB_FIXTURE:?GH_STUB_FIXTURE required}"
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -q -- '--jq .\[\].createdAt'; then
  grep -o '"createdAt":"[^"]*"' "$fixture" |
    sed 's/"createdAt":"//; s/"$//'
else
  cat "$fixture"
fi
STUB
chmod +x "$TMP/bin/gh"

RC=0
# run_check <event> <tag> <case-name> — runs the REAL check script against
# the stub with EVENT_NAME/GITHUB_REF_NAME set; the `dedupe=` line lands in
# $TMP/out.<case>, everything the script prints lands in
# $TMP/stdout.<case>, the stub's call log in $TMP/calls.log (fresh per
# case). The script's exit code is left in $RC.
run_check() {
  : > "$TMP/out.$3"
  : > "$TMP/stdout.$3"
  : > "$TMP/calls.log"
  EVENT_NAME="$1" GITHUB_REF_NAME="$2" GH_CALL_LOG="$TMP/calls.log" \
    PATH="$TMP/bin:$PATH" \
    bash "$CHECK" "$TMP/out.$3" >"$TMP/stdout.$3" 2>&1
  RC=$?
}

fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at rows...> — writes the
  # `gh run list --json createdAt` answer shape and prints its path.
  local name="$1"
  shift
  {
    printf '['
    local sep="" row
    for row in "$@"; do
      printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s"}' "$sep" "$row"
      sep=', '
    done
    printf ']\n'
  } > "$TMP/fx.$name"
  printf '%s' "$TMP/fx.$name"
}

# ── AC1: a fresh push twin dedupes the release twin ─────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture recent "$(iso_ago 60)")" run_check release vTest.0 fresh
check 'AC1: recent push run → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"
check 'AC1: the script exits 0 (the short-circuit is green, never red)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters this workflow (--workflow ci.yml)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--workflow ci.yml' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup keys on the tag ref (--branch <tag>)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--branch vTest.0' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: the lookup filters the push event (--event push)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--event push' "$TMP/calls.log"; echo $?)"
check 'RG: no --status filter — ANY status dedupes (the push twin is still in_progress in the hot path)' \
  "$(grep -q -- '--status' "$TMP/calls.log" && echo 1 || echo 0)"
check 'RG: the output file carries EXACTLY the dedupe line (annotations never pollute GITHUB_OUTPUT)' \
  "$(printf 'dedupe=true\n' | cmp -s - "$TMP/out.fresh"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1: 2+ runs, one stale + one recent — the recent one still dedupes ──
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture mixed "$(iso_ago 100000)" "$(iso_ago 120)")" \
  run_check release vTest.0 mixed
check 'AC1: a recent run among stale ones → dedupe=true' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.mixed"; echo $?)"

# ── AC1/AC2: the window boundary (default 6h) is honored ────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-in "$(iso_ago 21570)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-in
check 'AC1: a run seconds inside the window still dedupes' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=true' "$TMP/out.edge-in"; echo $?)"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture edge-out "$(iso_ago 21630)")" \
  DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS=21600 run_check release vTest.0 edge-out
check 'AC2: a run just past the window does NOT dedupe' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.edge-out"; echo $?)"

# ── AC2: the old-tag safety net ──────────────────────────────────────────
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture old "$(iso_ago 100000)")" run_check release vOld.0 old
check 'AC2: only stale push runs (old-tag release) → dedupe=false, the full gate runs' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.old"; echo $?)"

printf '[]\n' > "$TMP/fx.empty"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vNew.0 empty
check 'AC2: no push run at all (release-created tag) → dedupe=false' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.empty"; echo $?)"

# ── AC3: non-release arms never call the API ─────────────────────────────
for ev in push schedule workflow_dispatch; do
  GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check "$ev" vTest.0 "arm-$ev"
  check "AC3: $ev arm → dedupe=false" \
    "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.arm-$ev"; echo $?)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm makes NO gh call" \
    "$([ -s "$TMP/calls.log" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
  check "AC3: $ev arm exits 0" \
    "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"
done

# ── AC5: an API failure fails safe to the full gate ──────────────────────
GH_STUB_FAIL=1 GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$TMP/fx.empty" run_check release vTest.0 apierr
check 'AC5: gh run list failure → dedupe=false (the gate decides)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the failure warns loudly (::warning::)' \
  "$(grep -q '::warning::' "$TMP/stdout.apierr"; echo $?)"
check 'AC5: the script still exits 0 (the pre-check never reddens the run)' \
  "$([ "$RC" -eq 0 ] && echo 0 || echo 1)"

echo
if [ "$fails" -eq 0 ]; then
  echo '✅ release-dedupe self-test green'
  exit 0
fi
echo "❌ release-dedupe self-test: $fails failing assertion(s)"
exit 1

binaries:
    name: Build native binaries
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    needs: [release-dedupe, quality-gate]
    timeout-minutes: 45
    # Tag pushes (annotated, via PAT) and `release: published` events both
    # build the matrix. Since v0.1.370 the daily-publish plan creates
    # releases through the API — a lightweight tag with NO push event —
    # which silently starved linux/windows CLI assets (they existed only
    # while tags were still PAT-pushed, up to v0.1.369). The release event
    # fires for every creation path, so the matrix can never be starved
    # again.
    # gh-1625: on a deduped release twin the tag's own push run IS the
    # gate — the twin's quality legs all skip, so the explicit
    # `result == 'success'` check is ORed with the dedupe arm. The push
    # twin and the dedupe=false old-tag release still gate the matrix on
    # the full quality gate exactly as before.
    # Same !cancelled() pattern as the release job: the transitive skip
    # through always()-quality-gate starved this matrix on tag pushes and
    # release events alike (fa#456) — no linux/windows CLI assets since
    # v0.1.370. The explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from
    # building publishable binaries.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      (needs.quality-gate.result == 'success' ||
      (github.event_name == 'release' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe == 'true')) &&
      ((github.event_name == 'push' && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/v')) ||
      github.event_name == 'release')
    permissions:
      contents: write # attach assets to the GitHub Release
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - runner: windows-latest
            os: windows
            arch: x64
            archive: zip
          - runner: macos-latest
            os: macos
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
          # Intel Mac runner (macos-13 is retired; AOT cannot cross-compile
          # macos_x64 from arm64 — only linux_* targets cross).
          - runner: macos-15-intel
            os: macos
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          - runner: ubuntu-latest
            os: linux
            arch: x64
            archive: tar
          # Native ARM64 runner — dart build cli does not cross-compile.
          - runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            os: linux
            arch: arm64
            archive: tar
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      # gh-1522: the committed pubspec carries the 0.0.0-dev placeholder —
      # the TAG is the version (the retired flow compared tag vs pubspec
      # because a bot commit bumped the file; that commit path is gone).
      # Guard the placeholder here and stamp the bundle version from the tag.
      - name: Verify committed pubspec carries the placeholder
        # Explicit bash: the default shell on Windows runners is pwsh and
        # the POSIX test below dies there with a ParserError.
        shell: bash
        run: |
          placeholder=$(grep '^version:' pubspec.yaml | awk '{print $2}')
          if [ "$placeholder" != "0.0.0-dev" ]; then
            echo "::error::committed pubspec.yaml version is '$placeholder', expected the 0.0.0-dev placeholder (gh-1522) — a hand-bump desyncs the tag-derived builds. Revert pubspec.yaml."
            exit 1
          fi

      - run: dart pub get

    needs: [binaries, web-spa]

      github.event_name == 'release')

    steps:

      # present, so the signing job checks out the site/ tree.
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          mkdir -p provenance
          gh release download "${GITHUB_REF_NAME}" --repo "${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}" \
            --dir provenance --pattern 'fa-*'
          ls -l provenance

          cd provenance

          # The key never outlives the step — trap covers mid-step failure.

Let me first write the new selftest. Key parts to change:

1. Stub emulation. The check will run:
```
gh run list --workflow ci.yml --branch "$tag" --event push --limit 20 --json createdAt,conclusion,status --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt'
```
So `$*` contains `--jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt'`. 

Stub emulation:
```bash
if printf '%s' "$*" | grep -qF 'select(.conclusion'; then
  # Emulate `.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt`:
  # one createdAt line per SUCCESS run — other conclusions are filtered
  # out exactly like the real jq projection.
  grep -o '{"createdAt":"[^"]*","conclusion":"[^"]*","status":"[^"]*"}' "$fixture" |
    while IFS= read -r row; do
      case "$row" in
        *'"conclusion":"success"'*)
          printf '%s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$row" | sed 's/{"createdAt":"//; s/".*//')"
          ;;
      esac
    done
else
  cat "$fixture"
fi
```

Simpler with sed:
```bash
grep -o '{[^}]*}' "$fixture" | grep '"conclusion":"success"' | sed 's/.*"createdAt":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/'
```
Careful with ordering: `{"createdAt":"...","conclusion":"...","status":"..."}`. sed 's/.*"createdAt":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/' — greedy `.*` before `"createdAt":"` is fine since createdAt appears once. OK.

2. fixture() helper:
```bash
fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <created-at=conclusion=status rows...>
```
Hmm, better: keep positional rows but each row is `<created>` and optionally `:conclusion`. Let me design: `fixture <name> <spec>...` where spec = `<createdAt>` (defaults conclusion=success, status=COMPLETED) or `<createdAt>@<conclusion>@<status>`. Simple approach: separate args `--conclusion failure`. 

Cleaner: rows given as `createdAt:conclusion:status`, e.g. `"$(iso_ago 60):failure:COMPLETED"`. Default when missing fields: success/COMPLETED. Implementation:

```bash
fixture() { # fixture <case-name> <createdAt[:conclusion[:status]]>... — writes
  # the `gh run list --json createdAt,conclusion,status` answer shape and
  # prints its path. A bare timestamp defaults to a COMPLETED success run
  # (the normal hot-path answer: the push twin finished green).
  local name="$1"
  shift
  {
    printf '['
    local sep="" row created concl status
    for row in "$@"; do
      created="${row%%:*}"
      row="${row#*:}"
      if [ "$row" = "$created" ]; then
        concl="success"; status="COMPLETED"
      else
        concl="${row%%:*}"
        row="${row#*:}"
        if [ "$row" = "$concl" ]; then
          status="COMPLETED"
        else
          status="$row"
        fi
      fi
      printf '%s{"createdAt":"%s","conclusion":"%s","status":"%s"}' "$sep" "$created" "$concl" "$status"
      sep=', '
    done
    printf ']\n'
  } > "$TMP/fx.$name"
  printf '%s' "$TMP/fx.$name"
}
```

Wait, `${row%%:*}` on a bare timestamp `2026-...Z` — no colon → row unchanged, `${row#*:}` = row (no colon), so `row == created` → defaults. Good. For `t:failure` → created=t, row="failure", concl="failure", row="${row#*:}" = "failure" == concl → status=COMPLETED. For `t:failure:COMPLETED` → status=COMPLETED. Good.

3. AC1 case changes: `fixture recent "$(iso_ago 60)"` → needs to become `fixture recent "$(iso_ago 60)"` — a bare timestamp defaults to success. Keep.

4. New AC-1 fail-closed cases:
```bash
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture red "$(iso_ago 60):failure")" run_check release vTest.0 red
check 'FC: a recent FAILED push run does NOT dedupe (fail-closed: the full gate re-runs)' \
  "$(grep -qx 'dedupe=false' "$TMP/out.red"; echo $?)"
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture cancelled "$(iso_ago 60):cancelled")" run_check release vTest.0 cancelled
check 'FC: a recent CANCELLED push run does NOT dedupe' ...
GH_STUB_FIXTURE="$(fixture running "$(iso_ago 60)::IN_PROGRESS")" run_check release vTest.0 running
check 'FC: an in_progress push run does NOT dedupe (strictly safe: the concurrency queue means the push twin is completed by the time the release check runs; a sighting degrades to the full gate)' ...
```

Note `$(iso_ago 60)::IN_PROGRESS` → created=t, then row="" → concl="" → hmm: row="${row#*:}" on ":IN_PROGRESS" gives "IN_PROGRESS", concl="" … let me trace: row="t::IN_PROGRESS". created="${row%%:*}" = "t". row="${row#*:}" = ":IN_PROGRESS". Is row == created? No. concl="${row%%:*}" = "" (empty before colon). row="${row#*:}" = "IN_PROGRESS". Is row == concl? "IN_PROGRESS" == ""? No. status="IN_PROGRESS". So conclusion="" — bad. Use explicit `t:in_progress:IN_PROGRESS`? Wait what casing does gh use? gh run list --json conclusion returns lowercase ("success","failure","cancelled","skipped"), status returns UPPERCASE ("COMPLETED","IN_PROGRESS","QUED"). I'll use explicit values: `t:in_progress:IN_PROGRESS`. Hmm wait, `conclusion` for an in-progress run is null in the real API; jq select on null != success filters it out. My stub rows have no null support; using `"conclusion":""` or a literal would still not match success, so it's fine. I'll pass `t:in_progress:IN_PROGRESS` — conclusion `in_progress` is not realistic but the point (non-success does not dedupe) holds. Actually, cleaner to keep realism: conclusion empty. My parser: `t::IN_PROGRESS` → created=t, row=":IN_PROGRESS" → concl="" → row="IN_PROGRESS" ≠ concl → status="IN_PROGRESS". So `t::IN_PROGRESS` yields conclusion "", status IN_PROGRESS. Good — empty conclusion won't match success.

```bash
check 'RG: the lookup fetches conclusion+status (the decision is conclusion-aware)' \

check 'RG: only a GREEN push gate dedupes (fail-closed, gh-1625 review)' \

So the working tree DOES get the script file (git fetches missing blobs for the checkout). The "blobless" benefit is only that historical blobs aren't fetched. For depth 1 there's just one commit's blobs anyway.
