      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh","oldText":"    steps:

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

{"newText":"dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then","oldText":"dedupe=false

      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with

      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:

          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

{"newText":"dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then","oldText":"dedupe=false

blocks.text:
#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud

  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.

  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.

    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.

      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list

        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net

  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud

  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.

    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs

      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

          fetch-depth: 1

    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]

    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net

  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud

  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job, shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- Gated `if: github.event_name == 'release'` (the `release-pending` pattern): the checkout runs exactly on the arm that reaches the script, so push/dispatch/schedule arms still pay **no fetch** — AC3 discipline preserved.
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced with the correct one (a file-based check cannot work without a checkout; `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is inline).
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, gated to the release arm, ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

## Why the local suite missed it

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), so a checkout-loss regression reds `test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` (the checkout assertion) instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

{"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - id: check

        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job, shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- Gated `if: github.event_name == 'release'` (the `release-pending` pattern): the checkout runs exactly on the arm that reaches the script, so push/dispatch/schedule arms still pay **no fetch** — AC3 discipline preserved.
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced with the correct one (a file-based check cannot work without a checkout; `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is inline).
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copyright (c) 2026, the Flutter Agent Harness authors.
# Use of this source code is governed by a MIT license that can be found
# in the LICENSE file.
#
# release_dedupe_check.sh — the gh-1625 release-dedupe pre-check, run by
# the `release-dedupe` job of .github/workflows/ci.yml.
#
# The v* tag push fires the full quality gate by design (the release
# pipeline keys on the tag; the gate runs BEFORE anything publishes);
# the `release: published` event for the SAME tag fires a second,
# identical gate — observed on v1.0.580 (push run 38687023638 in_progress,
# release run 38687023803 pending behind it on the shared ci-<ref>
# concurrency group): doubled release wall time. This check decides
# whether the release twin may skip the gate:
#
#   release event AND a CI run for the same tag ref from the `push` event
#   exists with conclusion == "success" (FAIL-CLOSED, gh-1625 review: only
#   a GREEN push gate dedupes — behind the shared ci-<ref> concurrency
#   group the push twin is already completed when the release twin's
#   check executes, so any other outcome degrades to the full-gate safety
#   net below instead of letting a red tag ship binaries) created within
#   the last DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS (default 6h — the auto-release flow cuts
#   the tag and publishes the release seconds apart; the window bounds
#   the stale-republish edge)
#     → dedupe=true: every quality leg ANDs
#       needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true' into its `if` and
#       skips; the release twin keeps only its release-specific legs —
#       binaries-attach (idempotent --clobber upload, last wins),
#       release-provenance signing and installer smoke; web-spa/publish
#       stay keyed on the quality-gate result and skip with it;
#   anything else (no push run — a release cut on an old tag, or a tag
#   the release created itself: API-created tags fire no push event)
#     → dedupe=false: the release twin runs the full gate exactly as
#       before; that path stays the safety net (gh-1625 AC2).
#
# Fail-safe (gh-1625 AC5): dedupe defaults to false and flips only on a
# successful lookup — an `gh run list` error prints a ::warning:: and
# degrades to the full gate, never to a skipped one. The script never
# exits non-zero: a broken pre-check must not redden the run (same
# contract as gh-1551's release-pending check).
#
# Non-release arms (push/dispatch/schedule) short-circuit BEFORE any API
# call (gh-1625 AC3).
#
# Usage: release_dedupe_check.sh [output-file]   (default $GITHUB_OUTPUT)
# Contract: the output file receives EXACTLY one line `dedupe=<bool>`;
# annotations and logs go to stdout. The step maps the file into the
# job output consumed by every gate leg.
# Self-tested by scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh (PATH-stubbed gh);
# the workflow wiring is pinned by test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart.
set -u

out="${1:-${GITHUB_OUTPUT:?pass an output file or run inside a step}}"
EVENT_NAME="${EVENT_NAME:-}"
tag="${GITHUB_REF_NAME:-}"
window_secs="${DEDUPE_WINDOW_SECS:-21600}" # 6h

# ISO-UTC → epoch seconds: GNU date (Linux CI) and BSD date (local macOS).
iso_to_epoch() {
  date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null && return 0
  date -u -j -f '%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ' "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null
}

dedupe=false
if [ "$EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
  # The lookup the ticket prescribes: this workflow's runs for the tag
  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run
  # dedupes. A failed/cancelled push gate must re-gate here (the twin
  # goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the binaries job's
  # own "explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building
  # publishable binaries" invariant), never be waved through. The twin
  # twins share the ci-<ref> concurrency group with cancel-in-progress:
  # false, so by the time this check executes the push run is completed
  # and its conclusion is terminal — success-only is strictly safe. No
  # --repo flag (gh reads GH_REPO/GITHUB_REPOSITORY on the runner).
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
    echo "::warning::gh run list failed — fail-safe: the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC5)"
    printf '  %s\n' "$created_list"
  else
    now=$(date -u +%s)
    cutoff=$((now - window_secs))
    recent=""
    while IFS= read -r created; do
      [ -z "$created" ] && continue
      ts=$(iso_to_epoch "$created") || continue
      [ -z "$ts" ] && continue
      if [ "$ts" -ge "$cutoff" ]; then
        recent="$created"
        break
      fi
    done <<EOF
$created_list
EOF
    if [ -n "$recent" ]; then
      echo "::notice::a GREEN push CI run for $tag already gates this tag (created $recent) — the release twin skips every quality leg; binaries-attach, release-provenance and installer-smoke still run (gh-1625)"
      dedupe=true
    else
      echo "no push CI run for $tag within the last ${window_secs}s — the release twin runs the full quality gate (gh-1625 AC2 old-tag safety net)"
    fi
  fi
else
  echo "$EVENT_NAME arm — dedupe applies to release events only (gh-1625 AC3)"
fi

printf 'dedupe=%s\n' "$dedupe" >> "$out"

  # ref from the push event — conclusion-aware and fail-closed (gh-1625
  # review BLOCKING #2): ONLY a `conclusion == "success"` push run

#   the full gate runs exactly as before; that path stays the safety net
  #   (AC2).
  # Fail-safe (AC5): dedupe defaults false and flips only on a successful
  # `gh run list` — an API error degrades to the full gate with a loud
  # warning, never to a skipped gate; the pre-check never reddens the run.
  # AC3: non-release arms short-circuit in the script BEFORE any API call.
  # The concurrency rule below is untouched: the release twin still queues
  # behind the push twin (tag runs are never cancelled mid-flight) — it
  # just no longer re-runs the gate when its turn comes.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  release-dedupe:
    name: Release dedupe check (gh-1625)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      actions: read # gh run list — the push-run lookup for the tag ref
    outputs:
      dedupe: ${{ steps.check.outputs.dedupe }}
    steps:
      # The check runs a REPO script — a hosted runner's empty workspace
      # has no scripts/ and the first cut (no checkout) died with
      # `bash: scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh: No such file or directory`
      # (exit 127) on every arm, cascading into a red Quality gate (runs
      # 38696670029/38696668627). A file-based check needs a checkout; a
      # shallow + blobless one costs seconds inside the 5-minute budget.
      # Gated to the release arm — the only arm that reaches the script —
      # so push/dispatch/schedule arms keep paying no fetch (the
      # release-pending pattern; release-pending itself stays
      # checkout-free on non-schedule arms because its logic is INLINE).
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        env:
          EVENT_NAME: ${{ github.event_name }}
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh

  changes:
    name: Classify changes
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips the classifier too — every downstream leg is gated on
    # release-pending and would skip anyway, so classifying would be
    # wasted work (and a skipped classifier with empty outputs would
    # wave every changes-keyed leg past its path gate).
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
