Another check: the `changes` job — on a release event with dedupe=true, `changes` skips (pending=='true' but dedupe!='true' fails → skip). Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

One more consideration — the **`quality-gate` aggregate** itself: `needs` includes release-dedupe? The guard test pins `needs.first == 'release-pending'` and `needs[1] == 'release-dedupe'`. That passed. And quality-gate's `if` is `always() && pending && dedupe != 'true'`. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. There's precedent for inline logic in ci.yml being guard-tested via ci_release_pending_guard_test (which pins YAML text). And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Inlining would orphan the script file — I'd have to either delete it + rewrite the selftest to exercise the inline block (fragile), or keep the script as the source and have ci.yml inline a COPY (drift!). Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.

Option A (unconditional shallow+blobless checkout) is correct and simplest. The reviewer's suggested snippet (option 2) was exactly an unconditional checkout with fetch-depth: 1 + filter: blob:none. My "optimization" of gating it to the release arm broke the dispatch arms.

Let me reconsider the reviewer's option 1 (inline) once more, because the reviewer noted the invariant: "release-pending skips the fetch only because its logic is inline; a file-based check cannot work without a checkout (a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget)." They presented both as acceptable, and my guard-test pin of "never inlined" aligns with keeping the extracted script. With an unconditional checkout:
- Every arm pays seconds of fetch. The release-dedupe job runs on every PR-validation dispatch (every push to the PR) — an extra shallow fetch each time. This repo cares about CI cost (issue #177 "a PR pays only for what it touched") but a blobless shallow checkout is seconds and the job budget is 5 min. The reviewer explicitly blessed it.
- Correctness on all arms: script always present. ✓

So: remove the `if:` from the checkout step and fix the comment. Update the guard test: the checkout must NOT be gated (pin that it is unconditional — or at least pin it exists + precedes check; I'll pin `checkout['if']` is null with the reason "the check step runs on EVERY arm — the file must be provided on every arm (the af1396d3 dispatch-arm failure)").

Also update the selftest? The selftest tests the script, not the workflow — no change needed. The guard test is the one to re-pin. And update ci.yml comment (remove "Gated to the release arm" phrasing; explain unconditional: "the check step runs on EVERY event (no job-level if) — so the checkout must be unconditional; push/dispatch/schedule arms pay a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds), the price of keeping the decision extracted + fixture-self-tested").

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider option A vs a variant: conditional checkout that runs on all arms EXCEPT... no. The check step is unconditional; the file is needed everywhere. Unconditional it is.

Hmm, but wait — there's one more subtle alternative: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`? No — schedule needs it too (the check step runs on schedule arms as well and would 127).

So unconditional checkout, per the reviewer's exact option-2 snippet. Let me make the change, re-run the guard tests (the guard test currently pins `checkout['if'] contains "github.event_name == 'release'"` — that must flip to `isNull`), and re-run the selftest + full relevant set. The full suite job (sh-26) is running against the tree with the GATED checkout — its result will be stale for the guard test file. Per R6/R7: let it finish, treat as stale, then re-run deliberately. {"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job, shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- Gated `if: github.event_name == 'release'` (the `release-pending` pattern): the checkout runs exactly on the arm that reaches the script, so push/dispatch/schedule arms still pay **no fetch** — AC3 discipline preserved.
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced with the correct one (a file-based check cannot work without a checkout; `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is inline).
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, gated to the release arm, ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

## Why the local suite missed it

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), so a checkout-loss regression reds `test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` (the checkout assertion) instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.
","path":"outputs/review_replies/thread_1.md"}

{"content":"# Thread 2 — 🚨 BLOCKING: dedupe fires on ANY push-run status (fail-open)

**Fixed** — the decision is now conclusion-aware and fails closed, using your "simplest and strictly safe" variant: **dedupe only on `conclusion == "success"`**.

## What changed

`scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh`:

```bash
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
```

- A failed/cancelled push run now returns **no dedupe candidate** → `dedupe=false` → the release twin re-runs the full gate, goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the exact pre-PR invariant ("the explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building publishable binaries", gh-1537/gh-1172 gate-before-publish).
- Success-only is strictly safe given the concurrency queue (your analysis): behind the shared `ci-<ref>` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, the push twin is already **completed** when the release twin's check executes, so the in_progress case cannot arise in the hot path — and if it somehow did, degrading to the full gate is the safe direction. The status-blind justification ("push twin still in_progress") was wrong and is gone from the script, the workflow comments and the tests.
- AC5 fail-safe unchanged on top: an API error still warns and degrades to `dedupe=false`.

## Pinned (TDD, both red before the fix)

- `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` — new fail-closed fixtures on the two-era-faithful gh stub: recent `failure` → `dedupe=false`, `cancelled` → `dedupe=false`, `in_progress` → `dedupe=false`, and failure-among-stale-success → `dedupe=false` (plus the green fixtures still dedupe, windows/AC2/AC3/AC5 untouched — all were RED against the old script, now 24/24 green).
- `test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` — the `isNot(contains('--status'))` pin (thread 4) is replaced by a positive pin of the fail-closed projection: `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` must be fetched and `select(.conclusion == "success")` must filter it, with the concurrency-model reasoning in the reason text.

- **BLOCKING 2 — fail-open any-status dedupe**: the lookup is now conclusion-aware and fails closed — `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + `--jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt'`. Only a **GREEN** push gate dedupes; failed/cancelled push runs degrade to the AC2 full-gate safety net (the twin re-runs the gate, goes red, attaches nothing). While waiting, let me do a deeper sanity check one thing I want to be extra careful about: **AC3/AC4 interplay for the `installer-smoke` and `release-provenance` jobs on the deduped twin** — no changes made there, fine.

Another check: the `changes` job — on a release event with dedupe=true, `changes` skips (pending=='true' but dedupe!='true' fails → skip). Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

One more consideration — the **`quality-gate` aggregate** itself: `needs` includes release-dedupe? The guard test pins `needs.first == 'release-pending'` and `needs[1] == 'release-dedupe'`. That passed. And quality-gate's `if` is `always() && pending && dedupe != 'true'`. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. There's precedent for inline logic in ci.yml being guard-tested via ci_release_pending_guard_test (which pins YAML text). And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Inlining would orphan the script file — I'd have to either delete it + rewrite the selftest to exercise the inline block (fragile), or keep the script as the source and have ci.yml inline a COPY (drift!). Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.

Option A (unconditional shallow+blobless checkout) is correct and simplest. The reviewer's suggested snippet (option 2) was exactly an unconditional checkout with fetch-depth: 1 + filter: blob:none. My "optimization" of gating it to the release arm broke the dispatch arms.

Let me reconsider the reviewer's option 1 (inline) once more, because the reviewer noted the invariant: "release-pending skips the fetch only because its logic is inline; a file-based check cannot work without a checkout (a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget)." They presented both as acceptable, and my guard-test pin of "never inlined" aligns with keeping the extracted script. With an unconditional checkout:
- Every arm pays seconds of fetch. The release-dedupe job runs on every PR-validation dispatch (every push to the PR) — an extra shallow fetch each time. This repo cares about CI cost (issue #177 "a PR pays only for what it touched") but a blobless shallow checkout is seconds and the job budget is 5 min. The reviewer explicitly blessed it.
- Correctness on all arms: script always present. ✓

So: remove the `if:` from the checkout step and fix the comment. Update the guard test: the checkout must NOT be gated (pin that it is unconditional — or at least pin it exists + precedes check; I'll pin `checkout['if']` is null with the reason "the check step runs on EVERY arm — the file must be provided on every arm (the af1396d3 dispatch-arm failure)").

Also update the selftest? The selftest tests the script, not the workflow — no change needed. The guard test is the one to re-pin. And update ci.yml comment (remove "Gated to the release arm" phrasing; explain unconditional: "the check step runs on EVERY event (no job-level if) — so the checkout must be unconditional; push/dispatch/schedule arms pay a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds), the price of keeping the decision extracted + fixture-self-tested").

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider option A vs a variant: conditional checkout that runs on all arms EXCEPT... no. The check step is unconditional; the file is needed everywhere. Unconditional it is.

Hmm, but wait — there's one more subtle alternative: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`? No — schedule needs it too (the check step runs on schedule arms as well and would 127).

So unconditional checkout, per the reviewer's exact option-2 snippet. Let me make the change, re-run the guard tests (the guard test currently pins `checkout['if'] contains "github.event_name == 'release'"` — that must flip to `isNull`), and re-run the selftest + full relevant set. The full suite job (sh-26) is running against the tree with the GATED checkout — its result will be stale for the guard test file. Per R6/R7: let it finish, treat as stale, then re-run deliberately. Actually — the tree changed while it runs (I'm about to edit). R7 says never kill a running verification because files changed; let it finish and re-run. The full suite takes a while; I'll let it run and start a FRESH full-suite run after my edits …

A release-gated checkout would re-create the exit-127 failure on exactly the arm your log showed (`EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch`). - The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, **unconditional** (`if` is null — pinned with the dispatch-arm failure as the reason), ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), and the guard test pins the checkout that makes the step executable — a checkout-loss regression reds `dart test` instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

{"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        if: github.event_name == 'release'
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job, shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- Gated `if: github.event_name == 'release'` (the `release-pending` pattern): the checkout runs exactly on the arm that reaches the script, so push/dispatch/schedule arms still pay **no fetch** — AC3 discipline preserved.
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced with the correct one (a file-based check cannot work without a checkout; `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is inline).
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, gated to the release arm, ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), so a checkout-loss regression reds `test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` (the checkout assertion) instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

{"content":"# Thread 2 — 🚨 BLOCKING: dedupe fires on ANY push-run status (fail-open)

**Fixed** — the decision is now conclusion-aware and fails closed, using your "simplest and strictly safe" variant: **dedupe only on `conclusion == "success"`**.

## What changed

`scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh`:

```bash
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
```

- A failed/cancelled push run now returns **no dedupe candidate** → `dedupe=false` → the release twin re-runs the full gate, goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the exact pre-PR invariant ("the explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building publishable binaries", gh-1537/gh-1172 gate-before-publish).
- Success-only is strictly safe given the concurrency queue (your analysis): behind the shared `ci-<ref>` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, the push twin is already **completed** when the release twin's check executes, so the in_progress case cannot arise in the hot path — and if it somehow did, degrading to the full gate is the safe direction. The status-blind justification ("push twin still in_progress") was wrong and is gone from the script, the workflow comments and the tests.
- AC5 fail-safe unchanged on top: an API error still warns and degrades to `dedupe=false`.

{"content":"# Thread 2 — 🚨 BLOCKING: dedupe fires on ANY push-run status (fail-open)

**Fixed** — the decision is now conclusion-aware and fails closed, using your "simplest and strictly safe" variant: **dedupe only on `conclusion == "success"`**.

## What changed

`scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh`:

```bash
  if ! created_list=$(gh run list \
      --workflow ci.yml \
      --branch "$tag" \
      --event push \
      --limit 20 \
      --json createdAt,conclusion,status \
      --jq '.[] | select(.conclusion == "success") | .createdAt' 2>&1); then
```

- A failed/cancelled push run now returns **no dedupe candidate** → `dedupe=false` → the release twin re-runs the full gate, goes red on the same commit and attaches nothing — the exact pre-PR invariant ("the explicit gate check keeps failed-gate runs from building publishable binaries", gh-1537/gh-1172 gate-before-publish).
- Success-only is strictly safe given the concurrency queue (your analysis): behind the shared `ci-<ref>` group with `cancel-in-progress: false`, the push twin is already **completed** when the release twin's check executes, so the in_progress case cannot arise in the hot path — and if it somehow did, degrading to the full gate is the safe direction. Another check: the `changes` job — on a release event with dedupe=true, `changes` skips (pending=='true' but dedupe!='true' fails → skip). Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

One more consideration — the **`quality-gate` aggregate** itself: `needs` includes release-dedupe? The guard test pins `needs.first == 'release-pending'` and `needs[1] == 'release-dedupe'`. That passed. And quality-gate's `if` is `always() && pending && dedupe != 'true'`. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.

- Every arm pays seconds of fetch. The release-dedupe job runs on every PR-validation dispatch (every push to the PR) — an extra shallow fetch each time. This repo cares about CI cost (issue #177 "a PR pays only for what it touched") but a blobless shallow checkout is seconds and the job budget is 5 min. The reviewer explicitly blessed it.
- Correctness on all arms: script always present. ✓

So: remove the `if:` from the checkout step and fix the comment. Update the guard test: the checkout must NOT be gated (pin that it is unconditional — or at least pin it exists + precedes check; I'll pin `checkout['if']` is null with the reason "the check step runs on EVERY arm — the file must be provided on every arm (the af1396d3 dispatch-arm failure)").

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider option A vs a variant: conditional checkout that runs on all arms EXCEPT... no. The check step is unconditional; the file is needed everywhere. Unconditional it is.

Hmm, but wait — there's one more subtle alternative: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`? No — schedule needs it too (the check step runs on schedule arms as well and would 127).

So unconditional checkout, per the reviewer's exact option-2 snippet. Let me make the change, re-run the guard tests (the guard test currently pins `checkout['if'] contains "github.event_name == 'release'"` — that must flip to `isNull`), and re-run the selftest + full relevant set. I need to fix this properly. Options:

Another check: the `changes` job — on a release event with dedupe=true, `changes` skips (pending=='true' but dedupe!='true' fails → skip). Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

One more consideration — the **`quality-gate` aggregate** itself: `needs` includes release-dedupe? The guard test pins `needs.first == 'release-pending'` and `needs[1] == 'release-dedupe'`. That passed. And quality-gate's `if` is `always() && pending && dedupe != 'true'`. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. There's precedent for inline logic in ci.yml being guard-tested via ci_release_pending_guard_test (which pins YAML text). And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Inlining would orphan the script file — I'd have to either delete it + rewrite the selftest to exercise the inline block (fragile), or keep the script as the source and have ci.yml inline a COPY (drift!). Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.

Option A (unconditional shallow+blobless checkout) is correct and simplest. The reviewer's suggested snippet (option 2) was exactly an unconditional checkout with fetch-depth: 1 + filter: blob:none. My "optimization" of gating it to the release arm broke the dispatch arms.

Let me reconsider the reviewer's option 1 (inline) once more, because the reviewer noted the invariant: "release-pending skips the fetch only because its logic is inline; a file-based check cannot work without a checkout (a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget)." They presented both as acceptable, and my guard-test pin of "never inlined" aligns with keeping the extracted script. With an unconditional checkout:
- Every arm pays seconds of fetch. The release-dedupe job runs on every PR-validation dispatch (every push to the PR) — an extra shallow fetch each time. This repo cares about CI cost (issue #177 "a PR pays only for what it touched") but a blobless shallow checkout is seconds and the job budget is 5 min. The reviewer explicitly blessed it.
- Correctness on all arms: script always present. ✓

So: remove the `if:` from the checkout step and fix the comment. Update the guard test: the checkout must NOT be gated (pin that it is unconditional — or at least pin it exists + precedes check; I'll pin `checkout['if']` is null with the reason "the check step runs on EVERY arm — the file must be provided on every arm (the af1396d3 dispatch-arm failure)").

Also update the selftest? The selftest tests the script, not the workflow — no change needed. The guard test is the one to re-pin. And update ci.yml comment (remove "Gated to the release arm" phrasing; explain unconditional: "the check step runs on EVERY event (no job-level if) — so the checkout must be unconditional; push/dispatch/schedule arms pay a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds), the price of keeping the decision extracted + fixture-self-tested").

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider option A vs a variant: conditional checkout that runs on all arms EXCEPT... no. The check step is unconditional; the file is needed everywhere. Unconditional it is.

Hmm, but wait — there's one more subtle alternative: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`? No — schedule needs it too (the check step runs on schedule arms as well and would 127).

So unconditional checkout, per the reviewer's exact option-2 snippet. Let me make the change, re-run the guard tests (the guard test currently pins `checkout['if'] contains "github.event_name == 'release'"` — that must flip to `isNull`), and re-run the selftest + full relevant set. The full suite job (sh-26) is running against the tree with the GATED checkout — its result will be stale for the guard test file. Per R6/R7: let it finish, treat as stale, then re-run deliberately. Actually — the tree changed while it runs (I'm about to edit). R7 says never kill a running verification because files changed; let it finish and re-run. The full suite takes a while; I'll let it run and start a FRESH full-suite run after my edits …

{"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job; shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- **Unconditional, deliberately**: the `check` step itself has no job-level `if` (a skipped pre-check would empty its output), so it runs on EVERY arm — push/dispatch/schedule included. A release-gated checkout would re-create the exit-127 failure on exactly the arm your log showed (`EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch`). Every arm that can execute the step gets the file; the price is a seconds-level blobless fetch, the one you pre-approved ("fine for a 5-minute budget").
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced: `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is **inline**; this check is a repo file, and inlining it would orphan the fixture-self-tested script. The comment now documents exactly that trade.
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, **unconditional** (`if` is null — pinned with the dispatch-arm failure as the reason), ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

## Why the local suite missed it

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), and the guard test pins the checkout that makes the step executable — a checkout-loss regression reds `dart test` instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

The suite is still running (log empty because of `| tail -15` — output only flushes at the end). The full suite was reported as "+10984 passed, 10 skipped" in the PR description — it likely takes a while (maybe 10-30 min).

While waiting, let me do a deeper sanity check one thing I want to be extra careful about: **AC3/AC4 interplay for the `installer-smoke` and `release-provenance` jobs on the deduped twin** — no changes made there, fine.

Another check: the `changes` job — on a release event with dedupe=true, `changes` skips (pending=='true' but dedupe!='true' fails → skip). Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

One more consideration — the **`quality-gate` aggregate** itself: `needs` includes release-dedupe? The guard test pins `needs.first == 'release-pending'` and `needs[1] == 'release-dedupe'`. That passed. And quality-gate's `if` is `always() && pending && dedupe != 'true'`. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. There's precedent for inline logic in ci.yml being guard-tested via ci_release_pending_guard_test (which pins YAML text). And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Inlining would orphan the script file — I'd have to either delete it + rewrite the selftest to exercise the inline block (fragile), or keep the script as the source and have ci.yml inline a COPY (drift!). Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.

Option A (unconditional shallow+blobless checkout) is correct and simplest. The reviewer's suggested snippet (option 2) was exactly an unconditional checkout with fetch-depth: 1 + filter: blob:none. My "optimization" of gating it to the release arm broke the dispatch arms.

Let me reconsider the reviewer's option 1 (inline) once more, because the reviewer noted the invariant: "release-pending skips the fetch only because its logic is inline; a file-based check cannot work without a checkout (a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget)." They presented both as acceptable, and my guard-test pin of "never inlined" aligns with keeping the extracted script. With an unconditional checkout:
- Every arm pays seconds of fetch. The release-dedupe job runs on every PR-validation dispatch (every push to the PR) — an extra shallow fetch each time. This repo cares about CI cost (issue #177 "a PR pays only for what it touched") but a blobless shallow checkout is seconds and the job budget is 5 min. The reviewer explicitly blessed it.
- Correctness on all arms: script always present. ✓

So: remove the `if:` from the checkout step and fix the comment. Update the guard test: the checkout must NOT be gated (pin that it is unconditional — or at least pin it exists + precedes check; I'll pin `checkout['if']` is null with the reason "the check step runs on EVERY arm — the file must be provided on every arm (the af1396d3 dispatch-arm failure)").

Also update the selftest? The selftest tests the script, not the workflow — no change needed. The guard test is the one to re-pin. And update ci.yml comment (remove "Gated to the release arm" phrasing; explain unconditional: "the check step runs on EVERY event (no job-level if) — so the checkout must be unconditional; push/dispatch/schedule arms pay a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds), the price of keeping the decision extracted + fixture-self-tested").

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider option A vs a variant: conditional checkout that runs on all arms EXCEPT... no. The check step is unconditional; the file is needed everywhere. Unconditional it is.

Hmm, but wait — there's one more subtle alternative: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`? No — schedule needs it too (the check step runs on schedule arms as well and would 127).

So unconditional checkout, per the reviewer's exact option-2 snippet. Let me make the change, re-run the guard tests (the guard test currently pins `checkout['if'] contains "github.event_name == 'release'"` — that must flip to `isNull`), and re-run the selftest + full relevant set. The full suite job (sh-26) is running against the tree with the GATED checkout — its result will be stale for the guard test file. Per R6/R7: let it finish, treat as stale, then re-run deliberately. Actually — the tree changed while it runs (I'm about to edit). R7 says never kill a running verification because files changed; let it finish and re-run. The full suite takes a while; I'll let it run and start a FRESH full-suite run after my edits …

**Critical catch while re-auditing AC3**: the check step runs on **every** arm (no job-level `if`) — including the `workflow_dispatch` SM-validation arms where the CI failure was observed. My release-gated checkout would re-create exit 127 exactly there: on non-release arms the checkout is skipped and the script file is missing again. The checkout must be **unconditional** (the reviewer's original option-2 snippet). Fixing ci.yml and the guard pin:

{"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job; shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- **Unconditional, deliberately**: the `check` step itself has no job-level `if` (a skipped pre-check would empty its output), so it runs on EVERY arm — push/dispatch/schedule included. A release-gated checkout would re-create the exit-127 failure on exactly the arm your log showed (`EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch`). Every arm that can execute the step gets the file; the price is a seconds-level blobless fetch, the one you pre-approved ("fine for a 5-minute budget").
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced: `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is **inline**; this check is a repo file, and inlining it would orphan the fixture-self-tested script. The comment now documents exactly that trade.
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, **unconditional** (`if` is null — pinned with the dispatch-arm failure as the reason), ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

## Why the local suite missed it

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), and the guard test pins the checkout that makes the step executable — a checkout-loss regression reds `dart test` instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

Another check: the `changes` job — on a release event with dedupe=true, `changes` skips (pending=='true' but dedupe!='true' fails → skip). Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

One more consideration — the **`quality-gate` aggregate** itself: `needs` includes release-dedupe? The guard test pins `needs.first == 'release-pending'` and `needs[1] == 'release-dedupe'`. That passed. And quality-gate's `if` is `always() && pending && dedupe != 'true'`. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. There's precedent for inline logic in ci.yml being guard-tested via ci_release_pending_guard_test (which pins YAML text). And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Inlining would orphan the script file — I'd have to either delete it + rewrite the selftest to exercise the inline block (fragile), or keep the script as the source and have ci.yml inline a COPY (drift!). Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.

Option A (unconditional shallow+blobless checkout) is correct and simplest. The reviewer's suggested snippet (option 2) was exactly an unconditional checkout with fetch-depth: 1 + filter: blob:none. My "optimization" of gating it to the release arm broke the dispatch arms.

Let me reconsider the reviewer's option 1 (inline) once more, because the reviewer noted the invariant: "release-pending skips the fetch only because its logic is inline; a file-based check cannot work without a checkout (a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget)." They presented both as acceptable, and my guard-test pin of "never inlined" aligns with keeping the extracted script. With an unconditional checkout:
- Every arm pays seconds of fetch. The release-dedupe job runs on every PR-validation dispatch (every push to the PR) — an extra shallow fetch each time. This repo cares about CI cost (issue #177 "a PR pays only for what it touched") but a blobless shallow checkout is seconds and the job budget is 5 min. The reviewer explicitly blessed it.
- Correctness on all arms: script always present. ✓

So: remove the `if:` from the checkout step and fix the comment. Update the guard test: the checkout must NOT be gated (pin that it is unconditional — or at least pin it exists + precedes check; I'll pin `checkout['if']` is null with the reason "the check step runs on EVERY arm — the file must be provided on every arm (the af1396d3 dispatch-arm failure)").

Also update the selftest? The selftest tests the script, not the workflow — no change needed. The guard test is the one to re-pin. And update ci.yml comment (remove "Gated to the release arm" phrasing; explain unconditional: "the check step runs on EVERY event (no job-level if) — so the checkout must be unconditional; push/dispatch/schedule arms pay a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds), the price of keeping the decision extracted + fixture-self-tested").

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider option A vs a variant: conditional checkout that runs on all arms EXCEPT... no. The check step is unconditional; the file is needed everywhere. Unconditional it is.

Hmm, but wait — there's one more subtle alternative: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`? No — schedule needs it too (the check step runs on schedule arms as well and would 127).

So unconditional checkout, per the reviewer's exact option-2 snippet. {"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job; shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- **Unconditional, deliberately**: the `check` step itself has no job-level `if` (a skipped pre-check would empty its output), so it runs on EVERY arm — push/dispatch/schedule included. A release-gated checkout would re-create the exit-127 failure on exactly the arm your log showed (`EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch`). Every arm that can execute the step gets the file; the price is a seconds-level blobless fetch, the one you pre-approved ("fine for a 5-minute budget").
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced: `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is **inline**; this check is a repo file, and inlining it would orphan the fixture-self-tested script. The comment now documents exactly that trade.
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, **unconditional** (`if` is null — pinned with the dispatch-arm failure as the reason), ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

## Why the local suite missed it

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), and the guard test pins the checkout that makes the step executable — a checkout-loss regression reds `dart test` instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

{"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job; shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- **Unconditional, deliberately**: the `check` step itself has no job-level `if` (a skipped pre-check would empty its output), so it runs on EVERY arm — push/dispatch/schedule included. A release-gated checkout would re-create the exit-127 failure on exactly the arm your log showed (`EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch`). Every arm that can execute the step gets the file; the price is a seconds-level blobless fetch, the one you pre-approved ("fine for a 5-minute budget").
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced: `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is **inline**; this check is a repo file, and inlining it would orphan the fixture-self-tested script. The comment now documents exactly that trade.
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, **unconditional** (`if` is null — pinned with the dispatch-arm failure as the reason), ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

## Why the local suite missed it

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), and the guard test pins the checkout that makes the step executable — a checkout-loss regression reds `dart test` instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

blocks.text:
The suite is still running (log empty because of `| tail -15` — output only flushes at the end). The full suite was reported as "+10984 passed, 10 skipped" in the PR description — it likely takes a while (maybe 10-30 min).

While waiting, let me do a deeper sanity check one thing I want to be extra careful about: **AC3/AC4 interplay for the `installer-smoke` and `release-provenance` jobs on the deduped twin** — no changes made there, fine.

Another check: the `changes` job — on a release event with dedupe=true, `changes` skips (pending=='true' but dedupe!='true' fails → skip). Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

One more consideration — the **`quality-gate` aggregate** itself: `needs` includes release-dedupe? The guard test pins `needs.first == 'release-pending'` and `needs[1] == 'release-dedupe'`. That passed. And quality-gate's `if` is `always() && pending && dedupe != 'true'`. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. There's precedent for inline logic in ci.yml being guard-tested via ci_release_pending_guard_test (which pins YAML text). And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Inlining would orphan the script file — I'd have to either delete it + rewrite the selftest to exercise the inline block (fragile), or keep the script as the source and have ci.yml inline a COPY (drift!). Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.

Option A (unconditional shallow+blobless checkout) is correct and simplest. The reviewer's suggested snippet (option 2) was exactly an unconditional checkout with fetch-depth: 1 + filter: blob:none. My "optimization" of gating it to the release arm broke the dispatch arms.

Let me reconsider the reviewer's option 1 (inline) once more, because the reviewer noted the invariant: "release-pending skips the fetch only because its logic is inline; a file-based check cannot work without a checkout (a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget)." They presented both as acceptable, and my guard-test pin of "never inlined" aligns with keeping the extracted script. With an unconditional checkout:
- Every arm pays seconds of fetch. The release-dedupe job runs on every PR-validation dispatch (every push to the PR) — an extra shallow fetch each time. This repo cares about CI cost (issue #177 "a PR pays only for what it touched") but a blobless shallow checkout is seconds and the job budget is 5 min. The reviewer explicitly blessed it.
- Correctness on all arms: script always present. ✓

So: remove the `if:` from the checkout step and fix the comment. Update the guard test: the checkout must NOT be gated (pin that it is unconditional — or at least pin it exists + precedes check; I'll pin `checkout['if']` is null with the reason "the check step runs on EVERY arm — the file must be provided on every arm (the af1396d3 dispatch-arm failure)").

Also update the selftest? The selftest tests the script, not the workflow — no change needed. The guard test is the one to re-pin. And update ci.yml comment (remove "Gated to the release arm" phrasing; explain unconditional: "the check step runs on EVERY event (no job-level if) — so the checkout must be unconditional; push/dispatch/schedule arms pay a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds), the price of keeping the decision extracted + fixture-self-tested").

Wait — actually, hold on. Let me reconsider option A vs a variant: conditional checkout that runs on all arms EXCEPT... no. The check step is unconditional; the file is needed everywhere. Unconditional it is.

Hmm, but wait — there's one more subtle alternative: `if: github.event_name != 'schedule'`? No — schedule needs it too (the check step runs on schedule arms as well and would 127).

So unconditional checkout, per the reviewer's exact option-2 snippet. Let me make the change, re-run the guard tests (the guard test currently pins `checkout['if'] contains "github.event_name == 'release'"` — that must flip to `isNull`), and re-run the selftest + full relevant set. The full suite job (sh-26) is running against the tree with the GATED checkout — its result will be stale for the guard test file. Per R6/R7: let it finish, treat as stale, then re-run deliberately. Actually — the tree changed while it runs (I'm about to edit). R7 says never kill a running verification because files changed; let it finish and re-run. The full suite takes a while; I'll let it run and start a FRESH full-suite run after my edits …

**Critical catch while re-auditing AC3**: the check step runs on **every** arm (no job-level `if`) — including the `workflow_dispatch` SM-validation arms where the CI failure was observed. My release-gated checkout would re-create exit 127 exactly there: on non-release arms the checkout is skipped and the script file is missing again. The checkout must be **unconditional** (the reviewer's original option-2 snippet). Fixing ci.yml and the guard pin:

{"content":"# Thread 1 — 🚨 BLOCKING: `release-dedupe` fails on every run (script invoked without a checkout)

**Fixed** — kept the extracted script (option 2: a checkout step now provides it) and re-pinned the guard test in the same commit.

## What changed

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` — `release-dedupe` job:

```yaml
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          filter: blob:none # the check never reads blobs — one gh run list
      - id: check
        ...
        run: bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh
```

- Same repo-wide pinned SHA as every other job; shallow + blobless — seconds inside the 5-minute job budget.
- **Unconditional, deliberately**: the `check` step itself has no job-level `if` (a skipped pre-check would empty its output), so it runs on EVERY arm — push/dispatch/schedule included. A release-gated checkout would re-create the exit-127 failure on exactly the arm your log showed (`EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch`). Every arm that can execute the step gets the file; the price is a seconds-level blobless fetch, the one you pre-approved ("fine for a 5-minute budget").
- The wrong "no checkout, no actions" invariant comment was replaced: `release-pending` skips the fetch only because its logic is **inline**; this check is a repo file, and inlining it would orphan the fixture-self-tested script. The comment now documents exactly that trade.
- The extracted script stays the single source of truth (never inlined) so `scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh` keeps exercising the REAL decision.

## Guard updated in the same commit

`test/ci_release_dedupe_guard_test.dart` no longer pins the broken shape (`hasLength(1)` + `uses isNull`); it now pins the working contract: exactly one `actions/checkout` step, **unconditional** (`if` is null — pinned with the dispatch-arm failure as the reason), ordered before the `check` step, `fetch-depth: 1` + `filter: blob:none`.

## Why the local suite missed it

The selftest now also proves the lookup shape on a PATH-stubbed gh (`--workflow ci.yml --branch <tag> --event push`, `--json createdAt,conclusion,status` + the fail-closed projection), and the guard test pins the checkout that makes the step executable — a checkout-loss regression reds `dart test` instead of only surfacing on a hosted runner.

Legs keyed on `changes.outputs.*` then skip via their `if` needs.changes… wait — if `changes` is skipped, its outputs are empty, and legs with `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true'` evaluate to false → skip. All 30 legs were mechanically wired with the dedupe clause anyway. The PR's own "live dependency-graph simulation" covered this; and the guard test walks the closure. Fine.

Now — is there anything else in the CI failures file? Two runs (workflow_dispatch arm on the PR validation), both failing with the same two checks. My fix addresses the root cause. The `Quality gate` failure was collateral (skipped legs counted as dodge) — resolved once release-dedupe goes green (checkout present → script found → exits 0 → outputs dedupe=false on dispatch → gate legs run).

Wait — actually let me double check one subtle thing about the PR validation flow: the SM validation dispatch uses `workflow_dispatch` — the release-dedupe job runs (no job-level if), the checkout step is skipped (`if: github.event_name == 'release'` false), the check step runs `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` — the script EXISTS because the SM validation dispatch... hmm! Wait. Does the workflow_dispatch validation run have a checkout of the PR branch? The `release-dedupe` job itself has NO unconditional checkout now. On a workflow_dispatch arm, the workspace is EMPTY and the checkout is SKIPPED (gated to release). So `bash scripts/release_dedupe_check.sh` → **exit 127 again on the dispatch arm!**

Oh no. The thread-1 comment says the failure was observed on a plain `workflow_dispatch` arm (EVENT_NAME: workflow_dispatch in the CI log). AC3 says push/dispatch/schedule behavior unchanged — meaning those arms must run the check script (it short-circuits internally, prints "workflow_dispatch arm — dedupe applies to release events only"). The script must be FOUND on those arms too!

The `release-pending` precedent: its non-schedule arms have NO checkout and its logic is INLINE in the step (`run: |` block) — that's exactly why it works checkout-free. The reviewer's note: "its non-schedule arms are already checkout-free and inline for exactly this reason".

So my arm-gated checkout is WRONG: on dispatch/push/schedule arms the script file is missing → exit 127 → exactly the CI failure we're fixing, now on dispatch arms (which is precisely how the failure manifested on this PR!).

I need to fix this properly. Options:

A. Unconditional checkout (no `if`): every arm pays a shallow blobless fetch (~seconds). Simple, correct. AC3 "behavior unchanged" — the *outputs* are unchanged; a few seconds of fetch is a cost change, acceptable per the reviewer ("a blobless/shallow one costs seconds, fine for a 5-minute budget"). But it does alter the "non-schedule arms pay no fetch" property that the previous review comment (and my own comment text) touts...

B. Gate the checkout the OTHER way: run it whenever the script will run — i.e., on ALL arms (since the check step runs on every event). Same as A.

C. Inline the script logic into the step (option 1 from the reviewer) — mirrors release-pending; then non-schedule arms need no checkout. But then the extracted script + selftest must be restructured (selftest would test... the extracted script would no longer be used by ci.yml — drift risk), and the guard test's "extracted + fixture-self-tested, never inlined" pin would flip. The reviewer's option 1 says "move the ~40-line decision into the step's run: block". Then the selftest should extract the inline block? The sm_merge_guard_selftest pattern tests scripts/… hmm. There's precedent for inline logic in ci.yml being guard-tested via ci_release_pending_guard_test (which pins YAML text). And scripts/release_dedupe_selftest.sh + the static-gate wiring test pins "the selftest exercises the REAL script". Inlining would orphan the script file — I'd have to either delete it + rewrite the selftest to exercise the inline block (fragile), or keep the script as the source and have ci.yml inline a COPY (drift!). Bad.

D. Make the checkout conditional on "not a schedule arm"... pointless — schedule arms also run the check script (it short-circuits after printing). The script runs on EVERY arm (the check step is unconditional). So the checkout must be unconditional.
